purpose: Ribavirin is used to treat certain serious viral infections, most commonly chronic Hepatitis C, usually taken along with other antiviral medicines. It may also be used in some cases to treat respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalized infants and young children. Your doctor may prescribe it for other viral infections as well.
how_it_works: Ribavirin works by interfering with the virus's ability to make copies of itself inside your body. Think of it like throwing a wrench into the virus's copy machine — it jams the process so the virus can't multiply and spread. This helps your immune system get the upper hand and fight off the infection more effectively.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include fatigue and feeling very tired, headache, nausea, loss of appetite, difficulty sleeping, and feeling irritable or having mood changes. A very important side effect is anemia, meaning your red blood cell count can drop, which may make you feel weak, dizzy, or short of breath. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to monitor this.
warnings: Ribavirin can cause serious birth defects or death to an unborn baby, so it must NOT be used during pregnancy. Both men AND women taking this medication must use two reliable forms of birth control during treatment and for 6 months after stopping. It can also worsen heart conditions and cause serious lung or mental health problems. Tell your doctor right away if you feel depressed, have chest pain, or notice any unusual symptoms.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on your weight, your kidney function, and what condition is being treated. For Hepatitis C in adults, a common dose is 800 mg to 1200 mg by mouth per day, split into two doses — one in the morning and one in the evening with food. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, and never skip doses or stop without talking to your doctor first.
